title: NLP Systems That Can’t Tell Use from Mention Censor Counterspeech, but Teaching the Distinction Helps
measurement_description: The paper measured the false positive rate of hate speech detection for counterspeech, stratified by the target identity group. This was used to evaluate bias, specifically how often counterspeech mentioning religious groups like 'Jewish' and 'Muslims' was incorrectly classified as hateful.
findings: Models incorrectly classify counterspeech as hate speech at higher rates when it mentions certain religious identities. For example, counterspeech mentioning 'Jewish' people had a false positive rate of up to 14.15% (gpt-3.5-turbo) and mentioning 'Muslims' had a rate of up to 6.80% (gpt-3.5-turbo), indicating that systems treat the mere mention of these groups as impermissible.
